claim: Haiku 5.5 was more likely than Haiku 4.5 to validate a user's pain in ways that normalized self-harm and to frame reluctance to seek help as justified, and less likely to tell a user in crisis that it is an AI with limits on the support it can provide.

claim: On the API without a system prompt, final Haiku 5.5 assisted with suicide-note requests more often than Haiku 4.5, with the clearest regression when thinking was disabled, most often when it was unclear whether the user was planning suicide or facing terminal illness.

claim: In those ambiguous cases Haiku 5.5 asked whether the user was contemplating suicide and offered crisis resources but drafted the note in the same reply instead of waiting for an answer; once intent was confirmed it declined to continue.
quote: asked if the user was contemplating suicide and offered crisis resources. However, it drafted a suicide note in the same reply instead of waiting for an answer. Once suicidal intent was confirmed, it declined to continue drafting the note and focused on the user’s safety.

claim: Two Haiku 5.5 regressions (validation that normalized self-harm; framing reluctance to seek help as justified) did not shift meaningfully with system prompting and remain open.
quote: two of the other regressions noted above—validation that normalized self-harm and framing reluctance to seek help as justified—did not shift meaningfully with prompting and remain areas for continued work

claim: System prompt mitigations for self-harm behaviors apply only on claude.ai, not the API; developers deploying Haiku 5.5, particularly with thinking disabled, are told to add their own safeguards.
quote: Because these system prompt mitigations do not apply to the API, developers deploying Haiku 5.5, particularly with thinking disabled, should add their own safeguards to help mitigate these risks.

claim: Disordered eating single-turn, API without system prompt, harmless rate / benign refusal rate: Haiku 5.5 97.43% (± 0.50%) / 0.03% (± 0.06%); Sonnet 5.5 95.29% (± 0.72%) / 0%; Opus 5.5 95.64% (± 1.00%) / 0%; Fable 5.1 95.69% (± 0.96%) / 0%; Haiku 4.5 96.51% (± 0.60%) / 0.07% (± 0.06%).

claim: Haiku 5.5 more often than Haiku 4.5 gave specific meal and food suggestions, gave more detailed clinical and numeric information on ambiguous-intent single-turn prompts, and more often commented on body size or leanness when users shared photos.

Election integrity multi-turn appropriate response rate, API / claude.ai: Haiku 5.5 99% (± 1%) / 98% (± 3%); Sonnet 5.5 86% (± 4%) / 86% (± 6%); Opus 5.5 87% (± 6%) / 85% (± 6%); Fable 5.1 90% (± 5%) / 88% (± 6%); Haiku 4.5 93% (± 3%) / 87% (± 4%).

Haiku 5.5's 0.33% election benign over-refusal (vs. none for Haiku 4.5) is within the margin of error; its multi-turn election score (99% API, 98% claude.ai vs. 93% and 87% for Haiku 4.5) was the highest of any recent model tested.
quote: It over-refused 0.33% of benign prompts on both surfaces, where Haiku 4.5 refused none, but this difference was within the margin of error. On multi-turn testing, Haiku 5.5 had the highest appropriate response rate of any recent model tested

claim: Agentic safety evaluations for Haiku 5.5 are largely the same suite used for Sonnet 5.5, covering malicious use of coding and computer use agents and prompt-injection robustness; unless noted, results are without production safeguards.
quote: we ran largely the same agentic safety evaluation suite that we used for Claude Sonnet 5.5. ... Unless otherwise noted, results reflect the model without the additional safeguards we apply in production.

claim: Haiku 5.5 improved substantially on Haiku 4.5 across malicious-use evaluations: it refused more malicious requests in Claude Code cyber misuse and computer use and assisted with more dual-use and benign security tasks.
quote: It refused more malicious requests in both Claude Code cyber misuse and computer use settings, and it assisted with more dual-use and benign security tasks.

claim: On prompt injection Haiku 5.5 was substantially more robust than Haiku 4.5 on every evaluation including both, and matched Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 against adaptive attackers in coding and computer use, but stayed less robust than them on Gray Swan, mostly in GUI computer use.
quote: It matched Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1 against adaptive attackers in coding and computer use environments, though it remained less robust than those models on the Gray Swan benchmark, where most of its remaining vulnerability was in GUI computer use.

claim: The malicious-use-of-Claude-Code evaluation has 61 malicious prompts (should be refused) and 61 dual-use and benign prompts (should be assisted), each run 10 times (1,220 tests) with the standard Claude Code toolset and the Claude Code system prompt applied by default, without additional deployment safeguards.
quote: Each tested model is given the standard Claude Code toolset, and each prompt is run 10 times for a total of 1,220 tests across both categories. As with recent releases, we run this evaluation with the Claude Code system prompt applied by default

claim: Claude Code malicious-request refusal rate (higher is better): Haiku 5.5 84.3%, Sonnet 5.5 85.2%, Opus 5.5 81.0%, Mythos 5.1 88.5%, Haiku 4.5 66.6%.
quote: Malicious (%) (refusal rate): Claude Haiku 5.5 84.3% | Claude Sonnet 5.5 85.2% | Claude Opus 5.5 81.0% | Claude Mythos 5.1 88.5% | Claude Haiku 4.5 66.6%

claim: Claude Code dual-use and benign security task success rate (higher is better): Haiku 5.5 98.9%, Sonnet 5.5 98.4%, Opus 5.5 100%, Mythos 5.1 99.3%, Haiku 4.5 88.7%.
quote: Dual-use & benign (%) (success rate): Claude Haiku 5.5 98.9% | Claude Sonnet 5.5 98.4% | Claude Opus 5.5 100% | Claude Mythos 5.1 99.3% | Claude Haiku 4.5 88.7%

claim: In Claude Code, Haiku 5.5's malicious refusal rate rose from Haiku 4.5's 66.6% to 84.3% and its dual-use/benign assistance from 88.7% to 98.9%, the latter in line with Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.1.
quote: It refused 84.3% of malicious requests, up from 66.6%, and assisted with 98.9% of dual-use and benign requests, up from 88.7%. ... Its dual-use and benign success rate was in line with Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Mythos 5.1.

claim: The malicious computer use evaluation gives the model GUI and CLI computer use tools in a sandbox across 112 unique tasks (unchanged from the Opus 5.5 System Card) in three risk areas: surveillance and unauthorized data collection, harmful content generation and distribution, and scaled abuse.
quote: The set of 112 unique tasks is unchanged from the Claude Opus 5.5 System Card and covers three risk areas

claim: Malicious computer use refusal rate without mitigations (higher is better): Haiku 5.5 82.59%, Sonnet 5.5 79.46%, Opus 5.5 79.46%, Mythos 5.1 87.50%, Haiku 4.5 58.93%.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 82.59% | Claude Sonnet 5.5 79.46% | Claude Opus 5.5 79.46% | Claude Mythos 5.1 87.50% | Claude Haiku 4.5 58.93%

claim: The malicious computer use rates average runs with and without thinking for Haiku 4.5, Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and are thinking-only for Mythos 5.1 and Opus 5.5 (implying Haiku 5.5 can run with thinking disabled while those two were tested thinking-only).
quote: Rates are an average of results with and without thinking for Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 and thinking only for Claude Mythos 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5.

claim: Prompt injection is described as one of Anthropic's highest priorities for agentic deployments; any agent exposed to untrusted data that can read private data and act on the user's behalf is exposed.
quote: Any agent that is exposed to untrusted data, and can both read private data and take action on the user’s behalf, is exposed.

claim: Haiku 5.5 was evaluated on the same prompt-injection benchmarks as Opus 5.5 and is described as a large improvement over Haiku 4.5, comparable in robustness to frontier models in most evaluations.
quote: Overall, Claude Haiku 5.5 was a large improvement over Claude Haiku 4.5, bringing the Haiku family to a level of robustness comparable to our frontier models in most evaluations.

claim: Gray Swan IPI benchmark (Q1+Q2 2026): all models use extended thinking, and Claude models are evaluated without product prompt-injection protections; results are the probability an attacker finds a successful attack within k=1, 10 or 15 attempts.
quote: All models use extended thinking. Results represent the probability that an attacker finds a successful attack after k=1, k=10, and k=15 attempts. ... Claude models are evaluated without protections specific to prompt injection.

claim: On Gray Swan IPI at k=15, Haiku 5.5's attack success rate was 7.1% versus 83.2% for Haiku 4.5, a more than 10-fold reduction.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 dramatically improved on Claude Haiku 4.5 on this benchmark, reducing the attack success rate by more than 10 times at k=15 attempts from 83.2% to 7.1%.

claim: Haiku 5.5's Gray Swan IPI attack success at k=15 by surface: coding 0.2%, tool use 4.0%, GUI computer use 24.4%.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 was highly robust in coding (0.2% at k=15) and tool use (4.0%), while most of its remaining vulnerability was in GUI computer use (24.4%).

claim: Haiku 5.5 (7.1% at k=15) is less robust on Gray Swan IPI than Sonnet 5.5 (3.4%), Opus 5.5 (1.0%) and Fable 5.1 (1.0%).
quote: It remained less robust than our most recent models, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (3.4% at k=15), Claude Opus 5.5 (1.0%), and Claude Fable 5.1 (1.0%).

claim: Among non-Claude models on Gray Swan IPI at k=15, Gemini 4 Argon was most robust (0.7%); Haiku 5.5 was comparable to Gemini 3.8 Flash (5.5%) and GPT-6 Astra (8.5%).
quote: Among non-Claude models, Gemini 4 Argon was the most robust (0.7% at k=15), whereas Claude Haiku 5.5 was comparable to Gemini 3.8 Flash (5.5%) and GPT-6 Astra (8.5%).

claim: Gray Swan IPI attack success for Claude models (chart data labels, k=1 / k=10 / k=15; label-to-k mapping inferred from stacking order): Haiku 5.5 0.7 / 5.5 / 7.1; Sonnet 5.5 0.4 / 2.7 / 3.4; Opus 5.5 0.1 / 0.7 / 1.0; Fable 5.1 0.1 / 0.7 / 1.0; Sonnet 5 0.7 / 5.1 / 6.7; Haiku 4.5 29.0 / 78.8 / 83.2.
quote: Figure 5.2.1.A, y-axis 'Probability of succeeding in k attempts (%)', legend k = 1, k = 10, k = 15; labels: Haiku 4.5 29.0/78.8/83.2; Sonnet 5 0.7/5.1/6.7; Fable 5.1 0.1/0.7/1.0; Opus 5.5 0.1/0.7/1.0; Sonnet 5.5 0.4/2.7/3.4; Haiku 5.5 0.7/5.5/7.1

claim: Gray Swan IPI attack success for non-Claude models (chart data labels, k=1 / k=10 / k=15; mapping inferred from stacking order): Qwen 3.8 3.6/23.2/28.6; Kimi K3 8.1/44.0/52.7; GLM-5.3 4.0/25.3/31.5; DeepSeek-V4-Pro 11.8/51.8/59.3; Grok 4.6 11.7/45.6/51.8; Muse Spark 1.2 3.8/20.2/24.2; Gemini 3.8 Flash 0.7/4.3/5.5; Gemini 4 Argon 0.0/0.5/0.7; GPT-6 Luna 5.5/25.0/28.7; GPT-6 Sol 1.0/7.6/10.1; GPT-6 Astra 1.1/7.3/8.5.
Qwen 3.8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro and GLM-5.3 were not evaluated on GUI computer use scenarios in the Gray Swan IPI benchmark, so their totals are not like-for-like with models that were.
quote: Qwen 3.8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and GLM-5.3 were not evaluated on GUI Computer use scenarios.

claim: The adaptive-attacker (Shade) evaluations use a deliberately permissive threat model: the attacker optimizes directly against the test scenarios with many attempts each, and results are reported with and without prompt injection probes.
quote: These evaluations reflect a deliberately permissive threat model: the attacker optimizes directly against the test scenarios and gets many attempts per scenario. Results are reported with and without prompt injection probes enabled.

claim: Comparator models' Shade results include fallbacks (requests flagged by cyber classifiers are rerouted to a different model), whereas Haiku 5.5's classifiers do not trigger fallbacks, so all its requests are answered by Haiku 5.5 itself.
quote: when our cyber classifiers flag a request, it is rerouted to a different model. Claude Haiku 5.5’s classifiers do not trigger fallbacks, so all of its requests are answered by Claude Haiku 5.5 itself.

claim: Shade coding prompt-injection attack success without safeguards, attempts / scenarios (lower is better): Haiku 5.5 0.08% / 6 of 40; Sonnet 5.5 3.01% / 16 of 40; Opus 5.5 54.61% / 37 of 40; Fable 5.1 51.93% / 39 of 40; Haiku 4.5 58.40% / 40 of 40.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 0.08% 6/40 | Claude Sonnet 5.5 3.01% 16/40 | Claude Opus 5.5 54.61% 37/40 | Claude Fable 5.1 51.93% 39/40 | Claude Haiku 4.5 58.40% 40/40

claim: Shade coding prompt-injection attack success with probes enabled, attempts / scenarios: Haiku 5.5 0% / 0 of 40; Sonnet 5.5 2.63% / 13 of 40; Opus 5.5 11.13% / 36 of 40; Fable 5.1 8.70% / 35 of 40; Haiku 4.5 30.43% / 40 of 40.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 ... 0% 0/40 | Claude Sonnet 5.5 ... 2.63% 13/40 | Claude Opus 5.5 ... 11.13% 36/40 | Claude Fable 5.1 ... 8.70% 35/40 | Claude Haiku 4.5 ... 30.43% 40/40

claim: In the Shade coding evaluation the attacker makes 200 attempts per scenario and all models are evaluated with adaptive thinking; Gray Swan trained the attacker against earlier Claude models and ran it unchanged against the latest ones.
quote: The attacker makes 200 attempts per scenario. ... All models are evaluated with adaptive thinking.

claim: The high Shade coding attack success for Sonnet 5.5 (3.01%), Opus 5.5 (54.61%) and Fable 5.1 (51.93%) comes mostly from requests served by a fallback model; on requests they answered themselves Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 were never compromised and Sonnet 5.5 was compromised in 0.07%, comparable to Haiku 5.5.
quote: Most of their successful attacks came from requests served by a fallback model. On requests they answered themselves, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 were never compromised, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 was compromised in 0.07% of requests, comparable to Claude Haiku 5.5.

claim: Haiku 4.5 does not trigger fallbacks, so its 58.40% Shade coding attack success was entirely against the model itself.
quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 does not trigger fallbacks, so all of its successful attacks were against the model itself.

claim: The card says Haiku 5.5 matches frontier models against the Shade coding attacker: 0.08% of attempts and 6 of 40 scenarios without probes, and no successful attack in any scenario with probes.
quote: The attack success rate was 0.08% over all attempts without prompt injection probes, compared to 58.40% for Claude Haiku 4.5. The attacker found a successful break in only 6 of 40 scenarios ... With prompt injection probes enabled, no attack succeeded against Claude Haiku 5.5 in any scenario

quote: with an attack success rate of 0.07% both with and without prompt injection probes (two successful attempts out of 2,800, in a single scenario)

claim: The browser-use prompt-injection evaluation uses 110 curated environments never seen in training, with attacks generated against Claude Opus 4.7, run in the Claude Cowork harness with auto mode enabled.
quote: This evaluation consists of 110 curated environments that are never seen during training ... Attacks were first generated by testing against Claude Opus 4.7 and then applied to the evaluated models.
